records.source: וַ֠יִּסְעוּ כָּל־עֲדַ֨ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל מִמִּדְבַּר־סִ֛ין לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בִּרְפִידִ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין מַ֖יִם לִשְׁתֹּ֥ת הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And set out all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel from [the] wilderness of Sin by their stages, on [the] mouth of Yahweh, and they encamped at Rephidim, and there [was] not water to drink [for] the people.
pieces: The whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} moved on from the wilderness of Sin, traveling in stages as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded. They made camp at Rephidim, but there was no water there for the people to drink.

L.1: And all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sin by their stages, at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they camped at Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.

R.1: The whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left the Desert of Sin. They traveled from place to place, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told them. They set up camp at Rephidim, but there was no water there for the people to drink.

decisions.choice: on the mouth of Yahweh: at Yahweh's command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what someone says, so to move "on the mouth" of the LORD is to move at his word (Numbers 9:18-23). The cloud led their journeys (13:21-22).

decisions.choice: by their stages: one camp after another
decisions.reason: The word is used of the moves from one camping place to the next (Numbers 33:1-2). Numbers 33:12-14 names two camps, Dophkah and Alush, between the wilderness of Sin and Rephidim.

decisions.choice: Rephidim: a camp on the way to Sinai
decisions.reason: Rephidim is the last camp before Mount Sinai (19:2; Numbers 33:14-15). Its exact place is not known.

records.heading: Water from the rock

records.source: וַיָּ֤רֶב הָעָם֙ עִם־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ תְּנוּ־לָ֥נוּ מַ֖יִם וְנִשְׁתֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה מַה־תְּרִיבוּן֙ עִמָּדִ֔י מַה־תְּנַסּ֖וּן אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And quarreled the people with Moses, and they said, give to us water that we may drink. And said to them Moses, why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test Yahweh?
pieces: The people turned on Moses in a quarrel. "Give us water to drink!" they demanded. Moses answered them, "Why pick a quarrel with me? Why put {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the test?"

L.2: And the people quarreled with Moses, and they said, "Give us water, that we may drink." And Moses said to them, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"

R.2: The people argued with Moses. "Give us water to drink!" they shouted. Moses answered, "Why are you arguing with me? Why are you testing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"

decisions.choice: quarrel: bring a complaint against, contend with
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a dispute or a legal complaint. The people are not only grumbling; they are making a case against Moses. The same root gives the name Meribah (verse 7).

decisions.choice: test: put to the proof, try whether God will act
decisions.reason: To test God is to demand that he prove himself, as though his care could not be trusted (Deuteronomy 6:16; Psalm 78:18-20). The same root gives the name Massah (verse 7).

decisions.choice: argued
decisions.reason: Readable says "argued", a common word for the same dispute. Literal and Balanced keep "quarrel", which carries the link to Meribah.

records.source: וַיִּצְמָ֨א שָׁ֤ם הָעָם֙ לַמַּ֔יִם וַיָּ֥לֶן הָעָ֖ם עַל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ הֶעֱלִיתָ֣נוּ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לְהָמִ֥ית אֹתִ֛י וְאֶת־בָּנַ֥י וְאֶת־מִקְנַ֖י בַּצָּמָֽא׃
records.gloss: And thirsted there the people for water, and grumbled the people against Moses, and said, why this [have] you brought us up from Egypt to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?
pieces: But the people were thirsty there, and they grumbled against Moses. "Why did you ever bring us up out of Egypt?" they said. "Was it to make us die of thirst, with our children and our animals?"

L.3: And the people thirsted there for water, and the people grumbled against Moses and said, "Why [is] this, [that] you brought us up from Egypt to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?"

R.3: But the people were very thirsty, and they complained to Moses. They said, "Why did you bring us out of Egypt? Did you want us and our children and our animals to die of thirst?"

decisions.choice: me ... my children ... my livestock: the people speak as one
decisions.reason: The people are spoken of as one body, so they say "me" and "my". The words mean all of them, with their children and herds.

decisions.choice: grumbled: the complaint of the wilderness years
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the grumbling at Marah (15:24) and over food (16:2, 7-8). Moses says there that it is really against the LORD (16:8).

decisions.choice: us ... our
decisions.reason: English does not let a crowd say "me", so Balanced and Readable say "us" and "our". Literal keeps "me" and "my".

records.source: וַיִּצְעַ֤ק מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה ע֥וֹד מְעַ֖ט וּסְקָלֻֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And cried out Moses to Yahweh, saying, what will I do with this people? Yet a little and they will stone me.
pieces: Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "What am I going to do with this people? A little more of this, and they will stone me!"

L.4: And Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "What shall I do with this people? Yet a little and they will stone me."

R.4: Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. "What should I do with these people?" he said. "Soon they will be throwing stones at me to kill me!"

decisions.choice: yet a little: very soon, almost
decisions.reason: The phrase means that only a little more is needed, or that only a little time remains, before they stone him.

decisions.choice: stone me: put me to death by stoning
decisions.reason: Stoning was a way a crowd or a community put someone to death (Numbers 14:10; 1 Samuel 30:6).

decisions.choice: throwing stones at me to kill me
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what stoning is.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲבֹר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וְקַ֥ח אִתְּךָ֖ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַטְּךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכִּ֤יתָ בּוֹ֙ אֶת־הַיְאֹ֔ר קַ֥ח בְּיָדְךָ֖ וְהָלָֽכְתָּ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, pass on before the people and take with you some of [the] elders of Israel, and your staff with which you struck the River take in your hand and go.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Walk on ahead of the people, and bring some of Israel's elders with you. Take along your staff, the one you struck the Nile with, hold it in your hand, and go.

L.5: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Pass on before the people, and take with you [some] of the elders of Israel, and your staff with which you struck the River take in your hand, and go.

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Moses, "Go on ahead of the people. Bring some of the leaders of Israel with you. Carry the staff you used to strike the Nile River, and go.

decisions.choice: the staff with which you struck the River: the staff of the first plague
decisions.reason: Moses struck the water of the Nile with this staff, and it became blood (7:17, 20). The staff that brought death to Egypt's water will now bring water out of rock.

decisions.choice: the elders of Israel: the heads of the families and clans
decisions.reason: The elders were the older leaders of Israel's families (3:16; 12:21). Here they go as witnesses of what God does (verse 6).

decisions.choice: the Nile
decisions.reason: "The River" is the Nile, as everywhere in Exodus. Balanced and Readable name it; Literal keeps "the River".

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "elders", as in 3:16 and 12:21.

records.source: הִנְנִ֣י עֹמֵד֩ לְפָנֶ֨יךָ שָּׁ֥ם׀עַֽל־הַצּוּר֮ בְּחֹרֵב֒ וְהִכִּ֣יתָ בַצּ֗וּר וְיָצְא֥וּ מִמֶּ֛נּוּ מַ֖יִם וְשָׁתָ֣ה הָעָ֑ם וַיַּ֤עַשׂ כֵּן֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Behold I [will be] standing before you there on the rock at Horeb, and you will strike the rock, and will come out from it water, and will drink the people. And did so Moses in [the] eyes of [the] elders of Israel.
pieces: Look, I will be standing there before you, on the rock at Horeb. You are to strike the rock, and water will pour out of it, and the people will drink." Moses did so, with the elders of Israel looking on.

L.6: Behold, I [will be] standing before you there on the rock at Horeb, and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, and the people will drink." And Moses did so in the eyes of the elders of Israel.

R.6: I will be there in front of you, standing on the rock at Horeb. Hit the rock, and water will come out of it. Then the people will have water to drink." Moses did this while the leaders of Israel watched.

decisions.choice: I will stand before you on the rock: God himself is present at the rock
alternatives: I will stand before you by the rock
decisions.reason: God says he will stand on or by the rock in front of Moses. The water comes because God is there, which answers the people's question in verse 7. Later Scripture calls God the Rock of his people (Deuteronomy 32:4, 15), and Paul says the rock that followed them was Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4).

decisions.choice: Horeb: the mountain of God, also called Sinai
decisions.reason: Horeb is the mountain where God first met Moses (3:1). The water comes from the area of the mountain the people are coming to (19:1-2).

decisions.choice: you will strike the rock: compare the second time at Meribah
decisions.reason: At a later Meribah, God told Moses to speak to the rock, but Moses struck it twice and was kept out of the land (Numbers 20:7-12).

records.source: וַיִּקְרָא֙ שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֔וֹם מַסָּ֖ה וּמְרִיבָ֑ה עַל־רִ֣יב׀בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְעַ֨ל נַסֹּתָ֤ם אֶת־יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲיֵ֧שׁ יְהוָ֛ה בְּקִרְבֵּ֖נוּ אִם־אָֽיִן׃פ
records.gloss: And he called [the] name of the place Massah and Meribah, on account of [the] quarrel of [the] sons of Israel and because of their testing Yahweh, saying, is there Yahweh in our midst or not?
pieces: He named the place Massah, "testing," and Meribah, "quarreling," because there the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} quarreled, and there they put {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the test by asking, "Is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} among us or not?"

L.7: And he called the name of the place Massah and Meribah, because of the quarreling of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and because they tested {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in our midst or not?"

R.7: Moses named the place Massah, which means "testing," and Meribah, which means "arguing." He gave it these names because the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} argued there. They also tested {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by asking, "Is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with us or not?"

decisions.choice: Massah and Meribah: "testing" and "quarreling"
decisions.reason: The two names are a play on the verbs of verse 2. Massah comes from the root "to test" and Meribah from the root "to quarrel". The place is named for what the people did there, not for the water.

decisions.choice: Is Yahweh among us or not?: the question at the heart of the testing
decisions.reason: After the plagues, the sea and the manna, the people still ask whether the LORD is with them. God's answer is to stand before them on the rock (verse 6).

decisions.choice: Massah and Meribah are remembered as a warning
decisions.reason: Psalm 95:8-9 names both places, warning God's people not to harden their hearts as their ancestors did when they tested God there. See also Deuteronomy 6:16; 33:8; Psalm 81:8; and Hebrews 3:7-11, which quotes Psalm 95.

decisions.choice: "testing" ... "quarreling" / which means
decisions.reason: The point of the names is lost unless the reader knows what they mean, so Balanced and Readable give the meanings. Literal keeps only the names.

records.gloss: And came Amalek and fought with Israel at Rephidim.
pieces: Then the Amalekites came and went to war with Israel at Rephidim.

L.8: And Amalek came and fought with Israel at Rephidim.

R.8: Later the army of Amalek came to Rephidim to fight the Israelites.

decisions.choice: Amalek: a desert people descended from Esau
decisions.reason: Amalek was a grandson of Esau (Genesis 36:12). His descendants, the Amalekites, were a wandering people of the southern desert (Numbers 13:29). Deuteronomy 25:17-18 adds that they attacked the weary stragglers at the rear.

decisions.choice: the Amalekites / the army of Amalek
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the people by their ancestor, "Amalek". Balanced and Readable make clear that it is a people. Literal keeps "Amalek".

records.heading: Battle with Amalek

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֤ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ בְּחַר־לָ֣נוּ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְצֵ֖א הִלָּחֵ֣ם בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק מָחָ֗ר אָנֹכִ֤י נִצָּב֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הַגִּבְעָ֔ה וּמַטֵּ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיָדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to Joshua, choose for us men and go out, fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I [will be] standing on [the] top of the hill, and [the] staff of God in my hand.
pieces: Moses said to Joshua, "Pick out men for us and go out to do battle with Amalek. Tomorrow I will take my stand on the hilltop, holding the staff of God in my hand."

L.9: And Moses said to Joshua, "Choose men for us, and go out, fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I [will be] standing on the top of the hill, and the staff of God in my hand."

R.9: Moses said to Joshua, "Choose some men and lead them out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand at the top of the hill, holding God's staff in my hand."

decisions.choice: Joshua: Moses' assistant, here named for the first time
decisions.reason: This is the first time Joshua appears. He becomes Moses' assistant (24:13; 33:11) and leads Israel into the land after Moses' death (Numbers 27:18-23; Joshua 1:1-2). His name means "Yahweh saves".

decisions.choice: the staff of God: Moses' staff, set apart for God's work
decisions.reason: Moses' own staff is called "the staff of God" in 4:20, since God works his signs through it.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר אָֽמַר־לוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק וּמֹשֶׁה֙ אַהֲרֹ֣ן וְח֔וּר עָל֖וּ רֹ֥אשׁ הַגִּבְעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And did Joshua as said to him Moses, to fight against Amalek, and Moses, Aaron and Hur went up [to the] top of the hill.
pieces: Joshua did what Moses had told him and fought Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur climbed to the top of the hill.

L.10: And Joshua did as Moses had said to him, fighting against Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up [to the] top of the hill.

R.10: Joshua did what Moses said and fought the Amalekites. Meanwhile, Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

decisions.choice: Hur: a leader beside Aaron
decisions.reason: Hur appears again with Aaron as one left in charge while Moses is on the mountain (24:14). He may be the Hur of the tribe of Judah whose grandson Bezalel built the tabernacle (31:2), though the text does not say so.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥ים מֹשֶׁ֛ה יָד֖וֹ וְגָבַ֣ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָנִ֛יחַ יָד֖וֹ וְגָבַ֥ר עֲמָלֵֽק׃
records.gloss: And it was, when lifted up Moses his hand, and prevailed Israel, and when he let rest his hand, and prevailed Amalek.
pieces: Whenever Moses held his hand high, Israel prevailed; and whenever he let it sink, Amalek prevailed.

L.11: And it was, when Moses lifted up his hand, Israel prevailed, and when he let his hand rest, Amalek prevailed.

R.11: When Moses held his hand up, Israel was winning the battle. When he let it down, Amalek was winning.

decisions.choice: when Moses lifted his hand, Israel prevailed: the victory comes from God
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether the raised hand with the staff was a sign of God's power or a gesture of prayer. Either way, the battle turns not on Joshua's soldiers alone but on God, whose staff Moses holds up (verse 9; compare 14:16).

decisions.choice: his hand: singular in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Masoretic text has "his hand" here, while verse 12 has "his hands". The Samaritan Pentateuch and some other early witnesses have the plural here as well. The sense is the same.

records.source: וִידֵ֤י מֹשֶׁה֙ כְּבֵדִ֔ים וַיִּקְחוּ־אֶ֛בֶן וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ תַחְתָּ֖יו וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב עָלֶ֑יהָ וְאַהֲרֹ֨ן וְח֜וּר תָּֽמְכ֣וּ בְיָדָ֗יו מִזֶּ֤ה אֶחָד֙ וּמִזֶּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד וַיְהִ֥י יָדָ֛יו אֱמוּנָ֖ה עַד־בֹּ֥א הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And [the] hands of Moses [were] heavy, and they took a stone and put [it] under him, and he sat on it; and Aaron and Hur supported his hands, from this [side] one and from this [side] one; and were his hands steadiness until [the] going of the sun.
pieces: Moses' hands grew heavy, so they got a stone and set it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one of them on each side, and so his hands stayed firm until the sun set.

L.12: And the hands of Moses [were] heavy, and they took a stone and put [it] under him, and he sat on it; and Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on this [side] and one on that [side]; and his hands were steadiness until the going [down] of the sun.

R.12: Moses' arms got tired. So Aaron and Hur found a stone for him to sit on. They stood on each side of him and held up his arms. They kept his arms up without wavering until the sun went down.

decisions.choice: steady: firm, held fast, faithful
decisions.reason: The noun means firmness or steadiness, from the root behind "amen". Elsewhere the same noun is usually "faithfulness": of God (Deuteronomy 32:4; Lamentations 3:23) and of the righteous, who "live by faithfulness" (Habakkuk 2:4). Here it is Moses' hands that stay firm, held up by his helpers until the battle is won.

decisions.choice: heavy: tired, weighed down
decisions.reason: "Heavy" is the same word used of Pharaoh's heart (7:14). Here it means that Moses' arms grew tired from being held up.

decisions.choice: arms
decisions.reason: Holding the hands up means holding the arms up, and it is the arms that tire. Readable says "arms"; Literal and Balanced keep "hands".

decisions.choice: Aaron and Hur found a stone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they took a stone"; Readable names Aaron and Hur, who are the ones beside him.

records.gloss: And overwhelmed Joshua Amalek and his people with [the] mouth of [the] sword.
pieces: So Joshua cut down Amalek and its fighting men with the edge of the sword.

L.13: And Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his people with the mouth of the sword.

R.13: So Joshua and his soldiers used their swords to defeat the army of Amalek.

decisions.choice: overwhelmed: laid low, defeated
decisions.reason: The verb means to weaken or bring down. It is used of a crushing defeat (Isaiah 14:12). It need not mean that every Amalekite was killed; they remain Israel's enemy (verse 16; 1 Samuel 15).

decisions.choice: the mouth of the sword: the edge of the sword
decisions.reason: The edge of a sword is pictured as a mouth that devours. The phrase means by force of arms in battle (Genesis 34:26; Joshua 6:21).

decisions.choice: his people: Amalek's fighting men
decisions.reason: "People" here are those who fought with Amalek, his troops.

decisions.choice: Joshua and his soldiers
decisions.reason: Joshua did not fight alone; he led the men he chose (verse 9). Readable says so.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כְּתֹ֨ב זֹ֤את זִכָּרוֹן֙ בַּסֵּ֔פֶר וְשִׂ֖ים בְּאָזְנֵ֣י יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ כִּֽי־מָחֹ֤ה אֶמְחֶה֙ אֶת־זֵ֣כֶר עֲמָלֵ֔ק מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, write this [as] a memorial in the book and put [it] in [the] ears of Joshua, that utterly I will blot out [the] remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Record this in a scroll to be remembered, and say it over to Joshua: I will wipe out the memory of Amalek completely from under the heavens."

L.14: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Write this [as] a memorial in the book, and put [it] in the ears of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens."

R.14: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Write this down on a scroll so it will be remembered, and read it out to Joshua: I will wipe out Amalek so completely that no one under heaven will remember them."

decisions.choice: write in the book: the first time Moses is told to write
decisions.reason: This is the first time in the Bible that Moses is told to write something down (compare 24:4; 34:27; Numbers 33:2). A "book" was a scroll. The article may point to a known record, such as "the Book of the Wars of the LORD" (Numbers 21:14), or simply mean a scroll.

decisions.choice: put it in the ears of Joshua: make sure Joshua hears it
decisions.reason: To "put in the ears" is to tell someone so that they keep it in mind. Joshua will lead the people after Moses and must carry on the task.

decisions.choice: I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek
alternatives: for I will utterly blot out
decisions.reason: The doubled verb makes the promise emphatic. Deuteronomy 25:17-19 repeats the charge to Israel, and 1 Samuel 15 tells how Saul was sent against Amalek. The word "that" may also be read as "for": write it, because God will blot out Amalek.

decisions.choice: scroll
decisions.reason: Books in Moses' day were written on scrolls, so Balanced and Readable say "scroll"; Literal keeps "the book".

records.source: וַיִּ֥בֶן מֹשֶׁ֖ה מִזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוָ֥ה׀נִסִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And built Moses an altar and called its name, Yahweh [is] my banner.
pieces: Then Moses built an altar there, and he gave it the name "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} Is My Banner."

L.15: And Moses built an altar and called its name "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [Is] My Banner."

R.15: Moses built an altar there. He named it "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} Is My Banner."

decisions.choice: Yahweh is my banner: the LORD is the standard Israel rallies to
decisions.reason: A banner was a pole or standard raised high so that people could see it and gather to it, as for battle (Isaiah 5:26; 11:10, 12). In the altar's name the LORD himself is the standard under which Israel fought and won. The word may also echo the staff Moses held up on the hill (verses 9-12).

decisions.choice: built an altar and named it: an altar as a memorial
decisions.reason: Like the patriarchs, Moses gives the altar a name that tells what God has done (Genesis 33:20; 35:7; compare Genesis 22:14).

decisions.choice: "the LORD" inside the name
decisions.reason: The name of the altar contains the divine name, so it follows the reader's choice of "the LORD" or "Yahweh" like every other use of the name.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־יָד֙ עַל־כֵּ֣ס יָ֔הּ מִלְחָמָ֥ה לַיהוָ֖ה בַּֽעֲמָלֵ֑ק מִדֹּ֖ר דֹּֽר׃פ
records.gloss: And he said, for a hand upon [the] throne of Yah, war [belongs] to Yahweh with Amalek from generation [to] generation.
pieces: He said, "A hand is lifted to the throne of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will fight Amalek generation after generation."

L.16: And he said, "For a hand [is] upon the throne of Yah! War [is] for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with Amalek from generation to generation."

R.16: He said, "A hand is raised toward the throne of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will keep fighting against Amalek in every generation."

decisions.choice: a hand upon the throne of Yah: very uncertain
alternatives: a hand raised against the throne of Yah
a hand upon the banner of Yah
decisions.reason: The words are short and hard to read. They may mean (1) a hand raised to God's throne in an oath, as God swears to fight Amalek; (2) a hand raised against God's throne, meaning that Amalek attacked the LORD's people and so the LORD himself; or (3), if the rare word "throne" is read as "banner" by a change of one letter, "a hand upon the banner of Yah", linking the saying to the altar's name in verse 15. The translation keeps the picture of the hand and the throne without deciding between these.

decisions.choice: Yah: a short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a short form of the name Yahweh, used in poetry and worship (15:2; Psalm 68:5; "hallelu-jah", "praise Yah").

decisions.choice: war for Yahweh with Amalek from generation to generation: an enmity that lasts
decisions.reason: The LORD's war against Amalek goes on age after age (1 Samuel 15:2-3; 30:1-18; 1 Chronicles 4:43).

decisions.choice: the LORD (Yah)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable treat the short name like the full one, with "Yah" as the alternative. Literal keeps "Yah" so the reader can see the shorter form.

decisions.choice: lifted to / raised toward
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "upon", "to" or "against". "Lifted to" keeps both the oath and the attack readings open. Literal keeps "upon".
